concept:
Character concept for a 2D cut-out animation game. Draw ONE original creature: a coiling azure EASTERN DRAGON holding a round dragon pearl, the SECOND stage of a three-stage Wood evolution line whose first stage is image 6: the same little azure dragon grown into a long coiling dragon, in the same view and pose as image 1, coiled in a big loop above its clouds, one claw raised under its chin holding the pearl, on a plain white background. A cute, chunky creature, but an original design that must look clearly DIFFERENT from the figure the silhouette came from; not any existing character.

Image 1 (grey silhouette) and image 2 (the same figure split into numbered regions) show the PUPPET RIG the new creature will be animated on. They tell you where each part and joint is, NOT what the creature looks like: do not trace their outline. Viewer-left and viewer-right mean as seen in the picture.

KEEP FROM THE RIG (the animation moves these parts around these joints):
- the same parts, no more, no fewer, each where its numbered region is: 1 head with face; 2 small jade crown and white mane; 3 two horns and a whisker; 4 white mane tufts on the back; 5 coiled serpent body; 6 two arms; 7 hand holding the dragon pearl; 8 tail with a white tuft; 9 auspicious clouds;
- every joint where it is and every part pointing the same way as in image 1; eyes where the old eyes are;
- each part about the size and shape of its region; the whole figure about the same size.

CHANGE (the new look, region by region):
1 head with face: an eastern-dragon head of azure-teal scales facing the viewer-right with cream-yellow lips and chin, the back-of-skull spikes as small azure fins, one big golden-amber eye (one catchlight dot) exactly where the old near eye is, brow angled down, the far eye a thin golden sliver where the old one is; the lower jaw stays an open jaw with a cream-yellow lip, a dark red mouth and two small white fangs, a confident grin; no dark band under the eye, no bronze, no fire.
2 small jade crown and white mane: a small pale turquoise-jade crown with a thin coral-gold rim on top of the head where the bottom of the old crest is, and a tall flowing white mane plume streaming up and back behind it, about the size of the old crest; no helmet, no bronze, no spirals.
3 two horns and a whisker: two coral-gold antler horns (deer-antler shape with rounded tines): a long one sweeping back to the viewer-left where the old band is, a short one curling up on the viewer-right where the old curled horn is; the snout curl becomes one long thin white whisker curling forward from the tip of the snout.
4 white mane tufts on the back: three flowing white mane tufts sticking out from the back of the body loop in the same places and pointing the same way, like the white mane of image 6; no bronze, no blades.
5 coiled serpent body: the same long serpent body in azure-teal scales (a few simple scale arcs) with a cream-yellow belly stripe where the cyan stripes are; the chest is plain azure-teal with a cream-yellow belly front; no armor plate, no bronze, no patterns.
6 two arms: two slim azure-teal dragon arms with cream-yellow scales on the inner side; the TOP ends are the shoulders joining the body, the gold shoulder plates become round azure-teal shoulders; the viewer-left hand at the far end has three curved coral-gold claws; no armor, no bronze.
7 hand holding the dragon pearl: a round flat ivory-white dragon pearl where the old fist is (about the same size, a thin pale cream rim line, no glow, no shine), held by the dragon's hand: three curved coral-gold claws gripping its front.
8 tail with a white tuft: an azure-teal dragon tail with a cream-yellow underside rising the same way, its tip ending in a big flowing white hair tuft like the mane, where the old gold frame is; no gold frame, no crystal, no sparks, no loose diamond.
9 auspicious clouds: white auspicious clouds in the same places and sizes: flat white puffs of rounded swirl curls (ruyi curls) with a turquoise-jade band along the edges, a few turquoise swirl lines and thin turquoise trailing streaks; no cyan-blue fill.

ATTITUDE: a proud young dragon king ready to strike: brow angled down, a confident open-mouthed grin showing small fangs; cute, never scary, never a cheerful mascot.

{RENDER}
{DESIGN}
The style sheet is image 3; the hand-drawn map is image 4. Image 5 is an approved character of this game: copy its ink line weight and its pencil and crayon texture, not its design; it has a few white shine spots and some darker shading: do NOT copy those. Image 6 is the approved first stage of this creature: keep its colours, face and drawing style; this stage is the same creature grown up.

COLOURS: azure-teal blue scales (a clear blue leaning to teal, NOT green), a cream-yellow belly, a flowing white mane, coral-gold antler horns, long white whiskers, a small pale turquoise-jade crown with a coral-gold rim, big golden-amber eyes, a flat ivory-white dragon pearl, white auspicious clouds with turquoise-jade edges. Few colours.

AVOID: a green body or green scales, sky-blue or cyan clouds, a bronze helmet or crest with carved spiral patterns, heavy bronze armor plates, a yellow flame or a gold crystal frame on the tail, fire or lightning breath, bronze shoulder plates, a bronze chest plate, text, labels, numbers, the region colours, frames, background scenery, a second view, shading, shadows, white highlights, glossy shine, glow, gradients.
